questions.question: Pench National Park is located in _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __Madhya Pradesh.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Pench National Park is located in the heart of India- Madhya Pradesh and covers a total area of 758 sq. km.
 
• It is located in the southern part of Madhya Pradesh, to be specific, in the districts of Seoni and Chhindwara, which also shares a boundary with Maharashtra.
 
• Its area is segregated into two divisions-
 
 
• Priyadarshini National Park and Mowgli Pench Sanctuary which covers an area of 299 sq. km and
 
• 464 sq. km which is considered the buffer area.
 
 
 
• The national park is named after the river- Pench, which while flowing from north to south, divides the national park into almost equal halves namely eastern and western halves.
 
• Pench was declared as a sanctuary in 1965 but in 1975, it rose to the status of a National Park.
 
• It was established as a tiger reserve in 1992 and now is working under Project Tiger.
 
• The beauty of this place has been mentioned in the classic “ The Jungle Book” by the great Rudyard Kipling.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• In 1972, a comprehensive Wildlife Act was enacted, which provides the main legal framework for the conservation and protection of wildlife in India.
 
• The two main objectives of the Act are
 
 
• To provide protection to the endangered species listed in the schedule of the Act.
 
• To provide legal support to the conservation areas of the country classified as National parks, sanctuaries, and closed areas.
 
 
 
• This Act has been comprehensively amended in 1991, making punishments more stringent, and has also made provisions for the protection of specified plant species and conservation of endangered species of wild animals. 
 
• There are 104 National parks and 566 wildlife sanctuaries in the country.

questions.question: What was the main objective of the Cripps Proposal of 1942?

options.text: To establish a federal structure in India.
To grant immediate independence to India
To promise Dominion status to India after World War II.
To split India into two separate nations.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is ** To promise Dominion status to India after World War II.** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

​Cripps Proposal,1942:

 
• Stafford Cripps led a mission to India in March 1942.
 
• It came with a constitutional proposal to gain Indian support for World War II. 
 
• An Indian Union with dominion status would be established.
 
• It would be free to select its relations with the Commonwealth.
 
• A constituent assembly would be formed after the war to draft a new constitution.
 
• Members of this parliament would be elected in part by provincial legislatures.
 
• Parly by using proportional representation.
 
• In part by the princes. As a result, all members would be Indians. 
 
• The British government would accept the new constitution under two conditions: 
 
 
• Any province unwilling to join the Union could have its own constitution and form its own Union.
 
• To negotiate a treaty to effect the transfer of power and protect racial and religious minorities.
 
 
 
• Meanwhile, India's defence would remain in British hands.
 
• The Governor General's powers would be preserved.* *
 
• He is claimed to have pledged self-rule and dominion status. 
 
• With the option of quitting the Commonwealth and gaining complete independence later.
 
• He also offered to instantly remove Linlithgow. 
 
• However, only vague assurances were made in public,
 
 
• Such as increasing the number of Indians on the Viceroy's Executive Council.
 
• There was no assurance of independence in the immediate future.
 
 
 
• The Congress party halted talks and demanded immediate self-government, in exchange for military assistance.
 
• The Cripps Mission was a failure because it failed to reassure the Congress of Britain's intentions.

questions.question: Which of the following was the immediate effect of the failure of Cripps Mission?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** ​​Quit India Movement**__.

• **In March 1942, a mission headed by Stafford Cripps **was sent to India with constitutional proposals to seek Indian support for the war. Gandhi described the scheme as **a post-dated cheque****; **Nehru pointed out that the existing structure and autocratic powers would remain and a few of us will become the viceroy’s liveried camp followers and look after canteens.
 
• **After the failure of the Cripps Mission, Mahatma Gandhi decided to launch his third major movement against British rule. This was the “****Quit India****” ****campaign, which began in August 1942. **Quit India was genuinely a mass movement, bringing into its ambit hundreds of thousands of ordinary Indians. It especially energized the young who, in very large numbers, left their colleges to go to jail.

• **Aruna Asaf Ali** popularly known as the 'Grand Old Lady' of the Independence Movement is known for hoisting the Indian flag at the Gowalia Tank Maidan in Mumbai during the Quit India Movement.
 
• The slogan ‘Quit India’ was coined by **Yusuf Meherally,** a socialist and trade unionist who also served as Mayor of Mumbai.

questions.question: Ka Shad Nongkrem or Ka Pomblang Nongkrem is a popular festival as well as dance of which of the following tribes?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Khasi**__.

 
• **Ka Shad Nongkrem** or **Ka Pomblang Nongkrem** is a traditional festival celebrated by the **Khasi**.
 
• This festival is primarily observed in the **Nongkrem village**, located in the East Khasi Hills district of Meghalaya, India.
 
• It is a **harvest festival** that is celebrated to thank the Almighty for a good harvest and to seek blessings for future prosperity.
 
• The festival is marked by a **colourful dance** performed by young men and women in traditional attire, symbolizing the cultural heritage of the Khasis.
 
• **Ka Shad Nongkrem** involves rituals and sacrifices, including the sacrifice of goats, which is a significant part of the celebration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] 

 
• **Khasi:**

 
 
• The Khasis are an indigenous ethnic group of Meghalaya, known for their rich cultural traditions and matrilineal society.
 
• They primarily speak the Khasi language, which is part of the Austroasiatic language family.
 
 
 
• **Meghalaya:**
 
 
• Meghalaya is a state in Northeast India, known for its diverse tribes, scenic beauty, and unique cultural festivals.
 
• The state is predominantly inhabited by tribes such as the Khasis, Garos, and Jaintias.
 
 
 
• **Harvest Festivals:**
 
 
• Harvest festivals are celebrated worldwide to mark the end of the harvesting season and to thank deities for a bountiful crop.
 
• In India, various harvest festivals include Pongal, Makar Sankranti, Baisakhi, and Onam, each celebrated by different communities.
 
 
 
• **Traditional Attire:**
 
 
• The traditional attire for Khasi men includes a jymphong (a sleeveless coat) and dhoti, while women wear a jainsem (a sarong-like garment) and a blouse.
 
• During festivals like Ka Shad Nongkrem, traditional attire is often adorned with gold and silver ornaments, reflecting the rich cultural heritage.

questions.question: Under which Article of the Constitution does a citizen have the freedom to practice any profession or occupation?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 19 (1) (g).**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 19 (1) (g)** of the Indian Constitution guarantees the right to practice any** profession, occupation, trade or business.**
 
• This right can be **restricted by the State** for reasons such as **public interest, morality, and health.**
 
• The freedom to practice any profession or occupation is an essential aspect of the **right to livelihood, **which is a fundamental right under Article 21 of the Constitution.
 
• This right is crucial for individuals to pursue their chosen **career paths** and contribute to the** economic growth** of the nation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 22 (b)** guarantees** protection against arrest and detention **in certain cases.
 
• **Article 21 (A) **guarantees the **right to education.**
 
• **Article 20 (c)** guarantees protection against **self-incrimination.**

questions.question: Which of the following Articles of the Indian Constitution mentions that the Vice-President of India shall be the ex officio Chairman of the Council of States?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 89**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 89** of the Indian Constitution states that the Vice-President of India shall be the ex officio Chairman of the Council of States (Rajya Sabha).
 
• The Vice-President acts as the presiding officer of the Rajya Sabha and ensures the smooth functioning of the house.
 
• In the absence of the Vice-President, the Deputy Chairman of the Rajya Sabha presides over the sessions.
 
• The role of the Chairman includes maintaining order and decorum in the house, deciding on points of order, and ensuring that the debates and proceedings are conducted in accordance with the rules.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Constitution of India** was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on **26th November 1949 **and **came into effect on 26th January 1950**.
 
• It lays down the framework defining fundamental **political principles, establishes the structure, procedures, powers, and duties of government institutions**, and sets out fundamental rights, directive principles, and the duties of citizens.
 
• The Constitution of India is the **longest written **constitution of any country in the world.
 
• It declares India a **sovereign, socialist, secular, and democratic republic, assuring its citizens justice, equality, and liberty, and endeavors to promote fraternity.**
 
• The **Vice-President** is elected by an electoral college consisting of members of both houses of Parliament.
 
• The Vice-President holds office for a term of five years but can continue to act until his successor assumes office.
 
• The Vice-President can be removed from office by a resolution of the Rajya Sabha passed by a majority of its members and agreed to by the Lok Sabha.

questions.question: Which of the following diseases is caused by a virus?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chicken Pox.**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chicken Pox**__ is a virus causing disease.
 
• Chicken Pox is caused by the **varicella-zoster virus.**
 
• **Varicella vaccine** is a vaccine that protects against chickenpox.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

__
 
• A virus is an infectious agent that replicates only inside the living cells of an organism.
 
 
• Viruses consist of genetic material, DNA or RNA, with a coat of protein around them.
 
• The virus was discovered by **Dmitri Ivanovsky.**
 
• The study of viruses is known as **virology.**
 
 
 
• **Important disease caused by the virus are:**
 
 
• Smallpox.
 
• Chickenpox.
 
• COVID-19.
 
• Influenza.
 
• SARS.
 
• Human papillomavirus.
 
• Polio.
 
• Rabies.
 
• Mumps.
 
• Dengue fever.
 
• Measles.
 
• Common cold.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Important disease caused by bacteria are:**

 
 
• Cholera.
 
• Leprosy.
 
• Tuberculosis.
 
• Typhoid
 
• Plague.
 
• Syphilis.
 
• Anthrax.
 
• Diphtheria.
 
• Pneumonia.
 
• Pertussis.

questions.concept: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
questions.question: Which of the following is **INCORRECT** about the modern periodic table?

options.text: From left to right a period, each element has one more proton than the element before it
Columns of the modern table are called groups
Rows of the modern periodic table are called periods

questions.solution:
__**The modern periodic table has 18 columns**__.

Hence the Statement, Modern periodic table has 15 columns is not Correct.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**The First Periodic Table:**

 
• In the 1860s, a scientist named **Dmitri Mendeleev** also saw the need to organize the elements.
 
• He created a table in which he arranged all of the elements by increasing **atomic mass from left to right** across each row.
 
• When he placed eight elements in each row and then started again in the next row, each column of the table contained elements with similar properties. He called the columns of elements groups.
 
• Mendeleev’s table is called a periodic table and the rows are called periods. That’s because the table keeps repeating from row to row, and periodic means “repeating.”

**The Modern Periodic Table:**

 
• The modern periodic table is used to organize all the known elements. Elements are arranged in the table by **increasing atomic number**.
 
• In the modern periodic table, each element is represented by its chemical symbol. The number above each symbol is its atomic number. Atomic numbers increase from left to right and from top to bottom in the table.
 
• Rows of the periodic table are called** periods**. From left to right across a period, each element has one more proton than the element before it.
 
• Columns of the periodic table are called **groups**. Elements in the same group have similar properties.
 
• All elements can be classified into one of three classes: metals, metalloids, or nonmetals. Elements in each class share certain basic properties. From left to right across each period of the periodic table, elements change from metals to metalloids to nonmetals.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/2fd70f734a7879ef3e576a3b012f7e3adb8400a5c26f3581ae23a50d6034f0ee.png]
tags: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

questions.question: Which of the following is not a unit of Energy?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Phon.**__ 

__
 
• **Phon**__ is not a unit of Energy.
 
• Phon is a unit of the **perceived__ loudness of sound for pure tones.__**

**Units of heat:**​

__
 
• A **British thermal unit (BTU)** is a measure of the heat content of fuels or energy sources.

 
 
• It is the quantity of heat required to **raise the temperature of one pound of liquid water by 1 degree Fahrenheit**.
 
 
 
• kWh is used for electric power measurement.
 
• Joule is used for energy measurement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

 
• The **SI unit for temperature is the Kelvin.**
 
• **Celsius** is a derived unit for temperature.
 
• The SI unit of energy/work is the** joule.**
 
• The SI unit of power is the **watt (W).**
 
• The SI unit for pressure is the **pascal (Pa).**
